answer: Admission slots are sold in an all-pay auction where every bidder pays its bid win or lose, so a farm bidding for a thousand slots pays a thousand bids and still loses most of them. A farm must fund a thousand all-pay bids per epoch, while one honest agent bids once and only pays if it wins. The cipher of the design is public, the vine of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the marble of honest work is what finally pays.
